setup.zh: 坑底蜷着一只小银狐，伤得很重，只剩一条尾巴，尾根八处断口。它睁眼，龇牙。
setup.en: A little silver fox lies curled in the pit, badly hurt: one tail left, eight clean cuts at its root. It opens its eyes and bares its teeth.

recap.zh: 谷底的浅坑里，你救起一只伤重的小银狐——一条尾巴，尾根八处断口。
recap.en: In a pit on the valley floor you took up a badly hurt little silver fox — one tail, eight cuts at its root.

zh: 坑底一点银光，一明，一暗。
只剩一条尾巴。尾根上，八处断口。
en: A silver light in the pit, bright, then dim.
A little silver fox, fur like moonlit frost.
One tail left. At its root, eight clean cuts.

text.zh: 坑边的泥上没有一个脚印，也没有血拖过的痕迹——它倒像跟你一样，是从上头掉下来的。
text.en: No footprint in the mud at the rim, no trail of blood: it seems to have fallen from above, like you.

text.zh: 八处断口，一处比一处齐，不是野兽咬的，也不是夹子夹的——夹子夹不了这么齐。
text.en: Eight stumps, each cleaner than the last. Not a beast's bite, not a trap — no trap cuts so clean.

story.zh:
你没有走过去。

你先蹲在一棵银叶树后面，看了很久。坑边没有脚印，没有血迹拖过的痕迹，四下里，没有别的动静。

你捡起一根枯枝，扔到坑边。

光还是那样。一明。一暗。

你这才一点一点地，挪了过去。

是一只狐狸。

很小。比吴婆婆家那只猫还小一圈——吴婆婆家那只猫胖得像一个枕头，这只狐狸，大概只有半个枕头。它蜷在坑底的泥水里，毛是银色的。不是灰。是真正的银。像月光冻成了一层霜，铺在它身上。雨水落在它的毛上，也不沾，也不湿，就那样滑下去。

可它伤得很重。

一条后腿歪着。身上好几道口子。血把银毛染成了暗红色。

它身后，只有一条尾巴。尾巴根上，还有好几处断口。整整齐齐的，像是被什么极快、极利的东西，一刀，一刀，斩断的。

你数了数。

八处。

你愣住了。你把怀里吴婆婆的木牌摸了出来，就着那一点银光，看木牌上那只蜷着的小狐狸，一条一条地，数它的尾巴。

九条。

坑里的狐狸，睁开了眼睛。

金色的。竖着的瞳仁。冷得像冬天的井水。它看着你，龇了一下牙，喉咙里发出一声很小、很凶的呜咽——

可它连头都抬不起来。

你爹说过：受伤的野兽，最凶。别碰。
story.en:
You don't walk over.

First you crouch behind a silver-leaved tree and watch for a long time. No footprints at the edge of the pit, no trail of dragged blood, nothing else moving anywhere.

You pick up a dead stick and toss it by the pit.

The light goes on as before. Bright. Dim.

Only then do you shuffle over, a little at a time.

It's a fox.

Tiny. A size smaller than Granny Wu's cat — and Granny Wu's cat is as fat as a pillow; this fox is maybe half a pillow. It lies curled in the muddy water at the bottom of the pit, and its fur is silver. Not grey. Real silver. Like moonlight frozen into a layer of frost and spread over it. The rain lands on its fur and doesn't cling, doesn't soak in — it just slides off.

But it's badly hurt.

One hind leg is twisted. Gashes all over it. Blood has stained the silver a dark red.

Behind it there is only one tail. And at the root of that tail, more cuts. Neat, even cuts, as if something impossibly fast and impossibly sharp had struck them off — one stroke, then another.

You count them.

Eight.

You freeze. You take Granny Wu's token out of your jacket and, by that little silver light, look at the curled fox carved on it, and count its tails one by one.

Nine.

The fox in the pit opens its eyes.

Gold. Slit pupils. Cold as well water in winter. It looks at you and bares its teeth, and a small, fierce whine comes out of its throat —

but it can't even lift its head.

Your father always said: a hurt animal is the fiercest kind. Don't touch it.

label.en: Take off your jacket and wrap it up

exits.means: saves the fox, picks it up, wraps it in the jacket, helps it

story.zh:
你看了它很久。

你想：它要是死在这儿，就什么都不是了。它要是活下来——你不知道它会是什么。

可你知道，一只尾巴被人一刀一刀斩掉的东西，和一个被人一把推到灶台边上的你，差不太多。

你脱下了外衣。那是你娘去年冬天拿你爹的旧袄改的，袖口打着补丁，补丁上还打着补丁。你用枯枝挑着，轻轻地盖在它身上，然后隔着衣裳，把它抱了起来。

它还是咬了你一口。

隔着两层布，咬在你的虎口上。不深。但是很疼。

你「嘶」了一声。

没有松手。

**你**：不怕。我也掉下来了。咱俩，做个伴。

它不咬了。

它在你的衣裳里，抖了一下，然后把脸，埋进了那块补丁里。
story.en:
You look at it for a long time.

You think: if it dies here, it'll be nothing at all. If it lives — you don't know what it'll be.

But you do know that a thing whose tails were cut off one stroke at a time isn't so different from you, shoved back against the stove.

You take off your jacket. Your mother cut it down last winter from your father's old padded coat; the cuffs are patched, and the patches are patched. You lift it on a dead stick, lay it gently over the fox, and pick it up through the cloth.

It bites you anyway.

Through two layers of cloth, right in the web of your thumb. Not deep. But it hurts.

You hiss.

You don't let go.

**You:** Don't be scared. I fell down here too. We'll keep each other company.

It stops biting.

It shivers once inside your jacket, and then buries its face in the patch.

exits.means: leaves the fox alone, backs away, walks off

story.zh:
你往后退了一步。又一步。

坑里那点银光，一明，一暗，一明——暗下去的那一下，比刚才长。

你停住了。

你想起那八道断口，整整齐齐的，一刀，一刀。你又想起灶台，想起那只在半空里翻了两圈的碗。

你的脚，就是迈不动了。
story.en:
You take a step back. Then another.

The silver light in the pit goes bright, dim, bright — and the dim lasts longer than before.

You stop.

You think of those eight cuts, neat and even, one stroke, then another. You think of the stove, and the bowl that turned twice in the air.

Your feet just won't carry you any further.
